skill.name: agent-generation
skill.description: Generates guidance and templates for building project-specific Claude Code agents. It maps codebase analysis into focused tech stack, architecture, and domain experts.
skill.summary: Create focused Claude Code agent teams from real project structure and conventions.
skill.author: Cpicon

security_audit.summary: The static backtick, reconnaissance, and device-file alerts are false positives from Markdown documentation and read-only analysis examples. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. The remaining concern is that generated agent templates grant broad write, shell, and network tools by default.

remediation.issue: Generated agents receive broad tool permissions by default.
remediation.suggestion: Use the minimum tool set for each role and remove Bash, Write, Edit, WebFetch, or WebSearch unless that role clearly needs them.

remediation.issue: Documented shell snippets may be copied into sensitive repositories.
remediation.suggestion: Label shell examples as optional read-only inspection steps and advise users to review commands before execution.

static_findings.snippet: - **Files**: kebab-case for utils (`api-client.ts`), PascalCase for components (`UserProfile.tsx`)
- Check `lib/` services for business logic implementation
- `src/app/` - Next.js App Router pages and layouts
- **Global client state**: Use Zustand stores in `src/stores/`
- Check existing components in `src/components/` for patterns
- Use existing hooks from `src/hooks/` when available
- Add tests following patterns in existing `.test.tsx` files
- Use Tailwind utilities, avoid custom CSS
- **`references/agent-templates.md`** - Complete agent templates for each type

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Generated Agent Tool Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The skill template and examples assign generated agents broad tools including Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, and WebSearch. This can enable unnecessary file modification, shell execution, or network access if copied into agents without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The same broad tool list appears in the core template and all three example agents. The risk depends on downstream publication, but the evidence is direct.

content.value_statement: Generic assistants miss project conventions. This skill helps create specialized Claude Code agents using real architecture, domain, and tech stack details.
actual_capabilities: Defines principles for project-aware agents with distinct responsibilities.
Provides an agent structure template with triggers, system prompts, tool lists, colors, and model choices.
Maps tech stack, architecture, and domain analysis into recommended agent types.
Includes sample tech stack, architecture, and domain expert agents.
Provides read-only codebase analysis patterns for project type, conventions, and team sizing.
limitations: It does not execute agent generation by itself.
Example agents describe a sample Acme Dashboard project, not the user project.
Documented shell snippets should be reviewed before use in sensitive repositories.
It does not validate generated agents against tests or organization policy.

use_cases.title: Create an Agent Team for a New Repository
use_cases.description: Turn project structure, frameworks, and conventions into focused Claude Code agents for daily engineering work.

use_cases.title: Standardize Internal Agent Templates
use_cases.description: Use consistent fields, trigger rules, colors, and role boundaries across generated coding agents.

use_cases.title: Document Codebase Expertise Areas
use_cases.description: Convert architecture, technology, and business-domain knowledge into reusable assistant roles for team onboarding.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Basic Agent Team
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a small Claude Code agent team for my repository. Focus on tech stack and architecture agents first.

prompt_templates.title: Create Role-Specific Agents
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with known project areas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to generate separate agents for frontend, backend, architecture, and domain logic. Keep trigger conditions distinct.

prompt_templates.title: Tailor Agents to Existing Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the repository conventions and use this skill to draft agents that reference real directories, naming rules, and framework patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Large Project Agent Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a complex or multi-service repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an agent team for a large codebase. Balance coverage, avoid overlapping triggers, and recommend tool permissions per role.

output_examples.input: A Next.js dashboard needs agents for frontend patterns, file placement, and business entities.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a React expert, an architecture expert, and a domain expert with separate triggers and project-specific guidance.

output_examples.input: A monorepo has frontend, backend, shared packages, tests, and deployment files.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest a larger team with technology, architecture, testing, DevOps, and domain roles mapped to relevant project areas.

output_examples.input: A team wants reusable standards for generated Claude Code agents.
output_examples.output: The skill would provide consistent agent fields, color conventions, role boundaries, and prompt sections for every generated agent.

best_practices: Ground every generated agent in actual project files, frameworks, and conventions.
Keep trigger conditions specific so agents do not overlap unnecessarily.
Review tool permissions before publishing generated agents in shared environments.
anti_patterns: Publishing sample agents without replacing Acme Dashboard details.
Giving every generated agent shell, write, and network tools by default.
Creating broad agents with vague triggers and duplicated responsibilities.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It provides templates and guidance for generating project-specific Claude Code agents.

faq.question: Does it modify my repository automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and guidance. Another workflow must create or write agent files.

faq.question: Which agent types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers tech stack, architecture, domain, testing, DevOps, security, and performance agent patterns.

faq.question: Can it support large repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes team sizing guidance for monorepos, microservices, and complex projects.

faq.question: Are the examples ready to publish?
faq.answer: No. The examples use sample project details and should be replaced with real project knowledge.

faq.question: What should I review before using generated agents?
faq.answer: Review trigger scope, project-specific accuracy, and tool permissions for each generated agent.
